# Overview

## Package Description

The purpose of this package is to provide some utilities needed when accessing Unified User. Note that unlike most of the `@ps-refarch` packages, it does not provide CDK constructs, but rather utilities used in Lambda functions. The primary utility is the [`getAccessToken`](./functions/getAccessToken.html) function, which is used to get a Unified User M2M access token.

## Note on "environment" and "namespace" names

Many of the configuration items of this package's constructs talk about two similar-sounding and related names:
* The "environment name" (sometimes abbreviated as `envName`), which refers to a specific deployment of the Reference Architecture application in AWS.
* The "namespace", which refers to a level of deployments of the Reference Architecture application.

For most Reference Architecture applications, there are four "namespaces":
* `dev`, which is used by the development team for development purposes
* `int`, which is used primarily by the QA team, and is the primary place where QA testing is done
* `stgus`, which is also used primarily by the QA team, it is where all the applications can be seen together in one place, and we can test for (probably unwanted) interactions between them.
* `produs`, which is the production system seen by customers.

For anything past `dev`, the "namespace" is always the same as the "environment name". In `dev`, there are two options:
* The application's main branch is always deployed directly into the fixed `dev` environment. Like the other namespace/environments, there is only one `dev`.
* Developers can do personal or "feature branch" deployments to other environment names, all of which come under the `dev` namespace. Because we are following GitOps processes, the feature branch environment names are by convention the same as the git branch name, and always are prefixed by `dev/` since they are in the `dev` namespace. So a branch name might be `dev/ESP-1234`, which deploys into the `dev/ESP-1234` environment name (which is in the `dev` namespace).

## Note on "logical client ids"

When we talk about allocating Auth0 clients (needed to obtain M2M access tokens) to services, we needed to decide between a range of possibilities:

* At one end of the range, we could use separate Auth0 clients for every service. This would be the best for security (since this allows very fine-grained access control), but would be prohibitively expensive (since we need to pay for each and every M2M token issued from these clients).
* At the other end of the range, we could use the same Auth0 client for all services (e.g. all MFEs). This would be relatively lower cost, but would not be great for security (since this would not be least privilege regarding the services' access needs.)

We decided to take an approach which allows for either extreme, but which defaults to a "middle ground" that we think balances cost with security.

* We can give every service its own Auth0 client by assigning a separate `logicalClientId` property (see below) to each service. Typically something like the MFE id would be used.
* We can use the same client for all services by simply distributing the same Auth0 client credentials to all services/MFEs.
* The default behavior is expected to be to use the same Auth0 client for all services in the same account and region. This happens automatically, since the default `logicalClientId` if you don't specify one is called `common`.

# Installation

To install, add to your project:
```
npm install @ps-refarch/uu-utils
```

# Usage

## Examples

Here's a basic example of use of the [`getAccessToken`](./functions/getAccessToken.html) function. Something like this would be in your Lambda.

```typescript
  const audience = 'https://powerschoolcorp.com/svc/products/sis';
  const accessToken = await getAccessToken({
    namespace: psNamespace,
    districtUid: districtId,
    audience,
    authIssuer
  });
```

In addition, uu-utils needs to be able to reach infrastructure resources (see the **Necessary AWS Services** section below for details.).  By default, your stack's Lambda functions will not be able to interact with these resources unless you create applicable IAM grants.  If you're using the BffApi construct, these grants are available automatically for you by specifying **callsUnifiedUser:true** on your function.

```
    const bffApi = new BFFApi(myStack, 'myBffApi', {
      domain,
      functions: {
        'POST /my/function/url': {
          path: 'path/to/my/handler',
          handler: 'handler',
          cors: true,
          headers: 'content-type, superfetch',
          callsUnifiedUser: true,
          // other props go here...
        }
      }
```
If you're not using the BffApi construct and wish to use uu-utils in your Lambda function(s), you will need to manually apply Read grant to the Secrets Manager secret and ReadWrite to the DynamoDB token table.  

## Configuration

The following are the main configuration properties of [`getAccessToken`](./functions/getAccessToken.html).

|Key|Type|Meaning|
|---|----|-------|
|`namespace`|string|The "namespace" (see note above).|
|`districtUid`|string|The district/tenant/unified customer UID (also called MOTU GUID)|
|`audience`|string|The audience of the API to be called. The "audience" is a genericized name for the API and should not vary between different deployment environments. **NOTE**: unfortunately, for PS-SIS, the audience does depend on the deployment environment. This is an unfortunate mistake based on a misunderstanding of the purpose of the audience. For pre-production SIS environments, the `audience` is `https://powerschoolcorp.com/svc/products/sis`, while for production SIS environments, it is `https://powerschool.com/svc/products/sis`. See [this list of audiences and scopes](https://powerschoolgroup.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SHAREDSERVICES/pages/64926976898/API+Resource+Servers).|
|`scopes`|string|The requests scopes of the API to be called, if any. If not provided, a default set of scopes will be used. See [this list of audiences and scopes](https://powerschoolgroup.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SHAREDSERVICES/pages/64926976898/API+Resource+Servers).|
|`authIssuer`|string|The Auth0 issuer. Normally something like `https://int.auth.powerschoolcorp.com/` (for the `int` shared services environment).|
|`logicalClientId`|string|The logical client id to used. If not passed, assumes `common`.|

## Necessary AWS Services

The `getAccessToken` function uses the follow AWS service objects, which are created by the `account-region-configuration` repo.

* A DynamoDB table called the "token cache." This per-namespace table caches M2M tokens, since we pay for every M2M token generated by Auth0.
* A Secrets Manager secret to hold the Auth0 client credentials. The name of this secret is `token/{{getLogicalClientId}}/{{namespace}}`, e.g. `token/common/dev`. The value of this secret should be of the form `{clientId: string, clientSecret: string}` and is maintained manually.
